facts.statement: The genus Struthiomimus was described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1917.
facts.quote: authority: Osborn, 1917

facts.statement: Struthiomimus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now western North America.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus (meaning "ostrich mimic", from the Ancient Greek στρούθειος/stroutheios, meaning "of the ostrich", and μῖμος/mimos, meaning "mimic" or "imitator") is a genus of ornithomimid dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of what is now western North America.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus was a long-legged, bipedal dinosaur with a toothless beak.
facts.quote: They were long-legged, bipedal, ostrich-like dinosaurs with toothless beaks.

facts.statement: The abundance of fossils and the presence of a toothless beak suggest Struthiomimus was likely an omnivore rather than a pure carnivore.
facts.quote: Their overall abundance, in addition to their toothless beak, suggests that these animals were mainly herbivorous or (more likely) omnivorous, rather than purely carnivorous.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus likely foraged as an opportunistic omnivore, eating plants and small animals like mammals, reptiles, and insects.
facts.quote: Similar to the modern ostriches, emus, and rheas (among other birds), these dinosaurs likely lived as opportunistic omnivores, supplementing a largely plant-based diet with a variety of small mammals, reptiles, amphibians, insects, invertebrates, and anything else they could fit into their mouth, as they foraged.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe discovered the first remains of Struthiomimus in 1901 and initially named the species Ornithomimus altus.
facts.quote: In 1901, Lawrence Lambe found some incomplete remains, holotype CMN 930, and named them Ornithomimus altus

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton found by Barnum Brown in 1914 led to the creation of the new genus Struthiomimus in 1917.
facts.quote: However, in 1914, a nearly complete skeleton (AMNH 5339) was discovered by Barnum Brown at the Red Deer River site in Alberta, prompting O. altus to be described as the type species of a new genus, Struthiomimus, by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1917.

facts.statement: The type species Struthiomimus altus lived in the Late Campanian age of the Judithian stage.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus altus comes from the Late Campanian (Judithian age) Oldman Formation.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus altus was estimated to be about 4.3 meters long, 1.4 meters tall at the hips, and weigh around 150 kg.
facts.quote: The size of S. altus is estimated as about 4.3 m long and 1.4 m tall at the hips, with a weight of around 150 kg.

facts.statement: A larger specimen of Struthiomimus altus is estimated to have weighed about 233.8 kg.
facts.quote: A larger specimen of S. altus is estimated to weigh about 233.8 kg.

facts.statement: Specimens of the species Struthiomimus sedens measured 4.8 meters long and weighed 350 kg.
facts.quote: The specimens belonging to "S." sedens measured 4.8 m long and weighed 350 kg.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had a long neck that made up about 40% of the body length in front of the hips.
facts.quote: As with other ornithomimids, they had small slender heads on long necks (which made up about 40% of the length of the body in front of the hips).

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Struthiomimus consisted of ten neck, thirteen back, six hip, and about thirty-five tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Their vertebral columns consisted of ten neck vertebrae, thirteen back vertebrae, six hip vertebrae, and about thirty-five tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had a relatively stiff tail that was likely used for balance.
facts.quote: Their tails were relatively stiff and probably used for balance.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, Struthiomimus had three fingers of roughly equal length with only slightly curved claws.
facts.quote: As in other ornithomimids but unusually among theropods, the three fingers were roughly the same length, and the claws were only slightly curved

facts.statement: It is likely that Struthiomimus was covered in feathers all over its body.
facts.quote: It is likely it had feathers all over its body.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had hands that were longer relative to the humerus and possessed particularly long claws compared to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus had longer hands relative to the humerus than other ornithomimids, with particularly long claws.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus belongs to the family Ornithomimidae, which includes genera such as Anserimimus, Archaeornithomimus, Dromiceiomimus, Gallimimus, Ornithomimus, and Sinornithomimus.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus is a member of the family Ornithomimidae, a group which also includes Anserimimus, Archaeornithomimus, Dromiceiomimus, Gallimimus, Ornithomimus, and Sinornithomimus.

facts.statement: In 1976, Rinchen Barsbold classified ornithomimids within their own infraorder, Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: Rinchen Barsbold placed ornithomimids within their own infraorder, Ornithomimosauria, in 1976.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined fifty foot bones of Struthiomimus and found no signs of stress fractures.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, fifty foot bones referred to Struthiomimus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus was one of the first theropods to be envisioned as having a horizontal posture from the beginning of its discovery.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus was one of the first theropods envisioned from the outset as having a horizontal posture.

facts.statement: There is significant debate regarding the specific feeding habits of Struthiomimus.
facts.quote: There has been much discussion about the feeding habits of Struthiomimus.

facts.statement: Some theories suggest Struthiomimus may have been a shore-dwelling filter feeder.
facts.quote: Some theories suggest that it may have been a shore-dweller and may have been a filter feeder.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists argue Struthiomimus was likely a carnivore because it belongs to the theropod group, which is otherwise carnivorous.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists noted that it was more likely to be a carnivore because it is classified within the otherwise carnivorous theropod group.

facts.statement: The shoulder girdle of Struthiomimus did not allow for high arm elevation or low reaching.
facts.quote: The structure of the shoulder girdle did not allow a high elevation of the arm nor was optimised for a low reach.

facts.statement: The hand structure suggests Struthiomimus used its arms as a hook or clamp to bring branches or fern fronds to shoulder height.
facts.quote: This indicates that the hand was used as a "hook" or "clamp", for bringing branches or fern fronds at shoulder height within reach.

facts.statement: Struthiomimus could run at speeds estimated between 50 and 80 km/h.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have been able to run at speeds between 50 and 80 km/h.

facts.statement: Speed was Struthiomimus's primary defense mechanism against predators like dromaeosaurids and tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: The supposed speed of Struthiomimus was, in fact, its main defense from predators

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Struthiomimus might have used its hind claws to defend itself when cornered.
facts.quote: although it may also have been able to lash out with its hind claws when cornered

facts.statement: An unnamed younger species of Struthiomimus lived between 69 and 67.5 million years ago in the early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: A younger species (which has not yet been named), which apparently differed from S. altus in having longer, more slender hands, is known from several specimens found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation and lower Lance Formation, between 69 and 67.5 million years ago

facts.statement: Struthiomimus altus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 76 to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 76 y 70millones de años, durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: Struthiomimus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Struthiomimus fossils have been found in Alberta, Canada, and Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos se han encontrado en Alberta, Canadá y Wyoming, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: The genus Struthiomimus was named by Osborn in 1917.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1917

facts.statement: The species Struthiomimus altus was originally described by Lambe in 1902.
facts.quote: species_authority: (Lambe, 1902)

facts.statement: Struthiomimus was over 3 meters long but weighed little due to its hollow bones and light skeleton.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus medía más de 3m, sin embargo no pesaba mucho debido a sus huesos huecos y a la ligereza general de su esqueleto

facts.statement: An adult Struthiomimus reached about 4.3 meters in length, 1.4 meters in height at the hips, and weighed around 150 kg.
facts.quote: Un Struthiomimus adulto alcanzaba cerca de 4,3m de largo y 1,4 de alto hasta la cadera, pesando alrededor de 150kg

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Struthiomimus consisted of 10 neck vertebrae, 13 dorsal vertebrae, 6 sacral vertebrae, and about 35 tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Su columna vertebral constaba de 10vértebras del cuello, 13vértebras del dorso, 6vértebras de la cadera y unas 35vértebras de la cola

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had a toothless snout with a straight beak at the tip of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Tenía un hocico sin dientes que presentaba en la punta del premaxilar un pico recto

facts.statement: With its neck raised, Struthiomimus could reach a height of 2 meters.
facts.quote: Con el cuello levantado hacia arriba hubiera alcanzado los 2m en altura

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had relatively rigid tails that were likely used for balance.
facts.quote: Sus colas eran relativamente rígidas y probablemente las usaban para mantener el equilibrio

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, Struthiomimus had three fingers of approximately equal length with slightly curved claws.
facts.quote: Como en otros ornitomímidos, pero inusualmente entre los terópodos, los tres dedos tenían aproximadamente la misma longitud y las garras estaban ligeramente curvadas

facts.statement: It is probable that Struthiomimus was covered in feathers over its entire body.
facts.quote: Es probable que tuviera plumas por todo el cuerpo

facts.statement: The abundance of Struthiomimus fossils suggests it was likely a herbivore or omnivore rather than a carnivore.
facts.quote: Su abundancia sugiere que fue herbívoro u omnívoro en vez de carnívoro

facts.statement: Gastroliths were found in one specimen, which is common in herbivorous dinosaurs and may indicate a plant-based diet.
facts.quote: Además, en un espécimen se han hallado gastrolitos (piedras que ayudaban digerir la comida en el estómago cuando ésta no se trituraba), algo común en dinosaurios herbívoros

facts.statement: Remains of multiple individuals found together suggest Struthiomimus lived in herds.
facts.quote: También se han hallado restos de varios individuos juntos, lo que lleva a creer que estos dinosaurios vivían en manadas

facts.statement: The exact diet of Struthiomimus remains unknown, with various hypotheses circulating.
facts.quote: Sus hábitos alimentarios son todavía desconocidos y sobre ellos circulan varias hipótesis

facts.statement: It is debated whether Struthiomimus used its claws to grab fruit or branches, or to tear at prey.
facts.quote: de las cuales se teoriza que tal vez pudieron ayudar a agarrar frutas o ramas con hojas; sin embargo, también pudieron servir para desgarrar a sus presas

facts.statement: The upper beak edge of Struthiomimus was concave, unlike the straight-edged beak of Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: El borde del pico superior era cóncavo en Struthiomimus, a diferencia de Ornithomimus, que tenía bordes de pico rectos

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered an almost complete skeleton, cataloged as AMNH'5339, in 1914 at the Red Deer River deposits.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1914, un esqueleto casi completo, catalogado AMNH'5339, fue descubierto por Barnum Brown en los yacimientos del río Red Deer

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn officially described Struthiomimus as a separate genus in 1916.
facts.quote: fue oficialmente descrito como un género separado por Henry Fairfield Osborn en 1916

facts.statement: Dale Russell elevated Struthiomimus to a full genus in 1972.
facts.quote: Dale Russell convirtió a Struthiomimus en un género completo en 1972

facts.statement: In 2016, specimen ROM'1790 became the holotype for the new genus and species Rativates evadens.
facts.quote: En 2016, ROM'1790 se convirtió en el holotipo de un nuevo género y especie, Rativates evadens

facts.statement: Struthiomimus altus comes from the Upper Campanian Oldman Formation during the Judithian age.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus altus proviene de la Formación Oldman del Campaniano Superior, era Judithiano

facts.statement: Struthiomimus remains also come from the Late Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Restos de Struthiomimus provienen también de la Formación Dinosaur Park, que data de finales del Campaniense

facts.statement: Struthiomimus remains are found in the Late Campanian to Early Maastrichtian Horse Shoe Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: Hay restos de Struthiomimus procedentes de la Formación Cañón Herradura, la cual data de finales del Campaniense y comienzos del Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Some Alberta specimens were found in and under ash piles, suggesting a forest fire may have killed them.
facts.quote: De los especímenes hallados en Alberta, algunos fueron encontrados en y bajo pilas de ceniza, sugiriendo que un incendio forestal pudo haberlos matado

facts.statement: Struthiomimus is a member of the family Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus es un miembro de la familia Ornithomimidae

facts.statement: Anatomically, Ornithomimosauria represent the group of non-avian dinosaurs most closely related to ostriches.
facts.quote: Anatómicamente, los Ornithomimosauria representan el grupo de dinosaurios no avianos más estrechamente relacionados con las avestruces

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined fifty Struthiomimus foot bones for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2001 realizado por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, se examinaron cincuenta huesos del pie referidos a Struthiomimus en busca de signos de fractura por estrés, pero no se encontró ninguno

facts.statement: There is much debate regarding the feeding habits of Struthiomimus.
facts.quote: Hay mucha discusión acerca de los hábitos alimenticios de Struthiomimus

facts.statement: Due to its straight-edged beak, Struthiomimus is thought to have been probably omnivorous or herbivorous.
facts.quote: Debido a su pico de bordes rectos, se cree que Struthiomimus pudo ser probablemente omnívoro o herbívoro

facts.statement: Some theories suggest it was a shoreline dweller that ate insects, crabs, shrimp, and possibly dinosaur eggs.
facts.quote: Algunas teorías sugieren que pudo ser un habitante de orillas en las que comía insectos, cangrejos, camarones y posiblemente huevos de otros dinosaurios

facts.statement: Some paleontologists argue it was more likely a carnivore because it is classified within the theropod group.
facts.quote: Algunos paleontólogos señalan que es más posible que sea un carnívoro, ya que está clasificado dentro del grupo de los terópodos

facts.statement: This carnivore theory was not rejected until Osborn, who described and named the dinosaur, proposed it likely fed on tree buds, shrubs, and other plants.
facts.quote: Esta teoría no había sido rechazada hasta que Osborn, quien describió y nombró al dinosaurio, propuso que probablemente se alimentaba de yemas y brotes de árboles, arbustos y otras plantas

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Struthiomimus was herbivorous is supported by the unusual structure of its hands.
facts.quote: La hipótesis de que Struthiomimus era herbívoro encuentra sustento, además, en la estructura inusual de sus manos

facts.statement: The second and third fingers were the same length, could not function independently, and were likely joined by skin.
facts.quote: El segundo y tercer dedo tenían la misma longitud, no podían funcionar independientemente y es probable estuviesen unidos por piel

facts.statement: This indicates the hand was used as a "hook" to reach branches or fern fronds.
facts.quote: Esto indica que la mano fue utilizada como "garfio", para poner ramas o frondas de helecho a su alcance

facts.statement: The shoulder girdle structure did not allow high arm elevation nor was it optimized for low reach.
facts.quote: La estructura de la cintura escapular no permitía una gran elevación del brazo ni estaba optimizada para un alcance bajo

facts.statement: The hand could not fully flex for grasping or extend for raking.
facts.quote: La mano no podía flexionarse por completo para un movimiento de agarre o extenderse para rastrillar

facts.statement: This indicates the hand was used as a "hook" or "bracket" to bring branches or fern fronds to shoulder height.
facts.quote: Esto indica que la mano se usaba como "gancho" o "abrazadera", para poner al alcance ramas o frondas de helecho a la altura de los hombros

facts.statement: However, these adaptations could have been used for supporting wing feathers.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estas adaptaciones podrían haber sido utilizadas para el apoyo de las plumas de las alas

facts.statement: Struthiomimus had long hind legs similar to an ostrich, with the tibia being much larger than the femur.
facts.quote: Los miembros traseros de Struthiomimus fueron largos, muy parecidos a los de un avestruz, sobre todo porque la tibia era mucho más grande que el fémur

facts.statement: Its three metatarsals were fused together to transfer the force of the footstep from the legs to the rest of the body.
facts.quote: sus tres metatarsos estaban combinados entre sí para transferir la fuerza de la pisada desde las patas a las piernas y al resto del cuerpo

facts.statement: Struthiomimus relied on speed as its primary defense against predators such as dromaeosaurids like Saurornitholestes and Dromaeosaurus, and tyrannosaurids like Daspletosaurus and Gorgosaurus.
facts.quote: La supuesta velocidad del estrutiomimo fue, de hecho, su única defensa contra depredadores, como los dromeosáuridos, como Saurornitholestes y Dromaeosaurus y tiranosáuridos, como el Daspletosaurus y Gorgosaurus

facts.statement: It is estimated that Struthiomimus could run at speeds between 50 and 80 km/h.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que pudieron ser capaces de correr entre 50 y 80km/h

facts.statement: When taking 2 strides per second, the maximum stride length of Struthiomimus could reach 6 meters.
facts.quote: cuando daba 2zancadas por segundo la longitud máxima de estas pudo llegar a ser de 6m

facts.statement: Struthiomimus was one of the first coelurosaurs to organize its limbs, muscles, and tail like birds.
facts.quote: Struthiomimus fue uno de los primeros coelurosaurios en organizar sus extremidades, músculos y colas como las aves

facts.statement: Its tail acted more like a rudder to change direction at high speeds.
facts.quote: una cola que actuaba más como timón para cambiar de dirección a alta velocidad

facts.statement: Holding the femur more horizontally brought its legs forward and balanced the animal.
facts.quote: Sostener el fémur de manera más horizontal traía sus patas hacia adelante y equilibraba al animal

facts.statement: It is likely that Struthiomimus could not run as fast as modern ostriches because its long forelimbs and short tail made it heavier.
facts.quote: muy probablemente no pudo alcanzar esta capacidad al ritmo que lo hacen las avestruces modernas, debido a que sus largas patas delanteras y su cola corta lo hacían más pesado
